content:
What is the reason that Lean uses DTT over ZFC Set Theory?
I understand why we use ZFC Set Theory outside Lean4 though, which has made me ask about Lean4 specifically.

Best,
Amlal

Interesting way to ask it ! I wonder if you could be more specific in “ I understand why we use ZFC set theory outside of lean “.

Depending what you mean by this , cause it’s kind of debatable IMO, there may be a quicker way to explain it .

But honestly the true answer can span pages of theoretical and historical context , at least in my view .

Keep in mind FOL axiomatic set theories can be used for automated theorem proving and have been, ZFC is also formalised within Lean , and most theorem provers do not use dependent types. So if there was an obvious and clear benefit and answer as to why, you’d expect it to homogenise to this standard somewhat .

Hey,

Interesting way to ask it ! I wonder if you could be more specific in “ I understand why we use ZFC set theory outside of lean “. Depending what you mean by this

So when I mentioned "I understand why we use ZFC set theory outside of lean" I meant in the general practice of Mathematics, in papers for example.

Keep in mind FOL axiomatic set theories can be used for automated theorem proving and have been, ZFC is also formalised within Lean , and most theorem provers do not use dependent types. So if there was an obvious and clear benefit and answer as to why, you’d expect it to homogenise to this standard somewhat .

Oh, so then it uses different tactics to perform the solving?
Using type theory is not at all specific to Lean (for example Rocq and Isabelle also use type theory). This beautiful answer by @Andrej Bauer gives some insights.

Hi Riccardo, I'll have a look at the MathOverflow link, thanks for sharing it.
Let me know if I can DM you if I have some questions?

If you want to know super specifically why “dependent “ , I’ll try find something analogous to that blog.

@Amlal El Mahrouss It's usually better to ask this kind of questions here, as many experts will read them. The link explains why type theory is used by most modern proof assistant instead of set theory. The question about simple type theory against dependent type theory is probably a little more nuanced, but the general philosophy is probably the same: in practice it often works better (this doesn't mean that it's impossible to use simple type theory or set theory of course).

@Riccardo Brasca While I'm re-reading the link you sent in the chat, I'm starting to understand the why of the rationale here.
And speaking of the questions, yes I'll keep them here then.

Thanks @Riccardo Brasca @Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 for your help! It means a lot.
You can have a look at this presentation by Leonardo de Moura where he explains why he decided to go with dependent type theory. Here is the video.
Okay, will have a look at it in 2hrs~ after I finish taking some notes. Thanks.
just a naive question. what would be "defeq" in ZFC?

There is also a concept that truly helped me understand more , especially as I used lean and actually ran into it wanting to pull my hair out .

It is called “Dependent type theory hell” colloquially , and I’ve tried to find some resources explaining it…it seems really hard to find using the new shit Google engine.

@Riccardo Brasca do you happen to know a place explaining or show casing it well? It might be cool to see “why not dependent types” too. Best I got is https://lawrencecpaulson.github.io//2026/04/23/Why_not_Lean.html

For DTT hell? You can see it in action in definitions like HomologicalComplex. The reason why we have differentials going from any X.i to any X.j it's just because if you write the naïve one you very quickly run into it.

Jiaxi Mo said:

just a naive question. what would be "defeq" in ZFC?

Nothing in the traditional sense it is FOL axiomatic theory + choice with a urelement and Set or something along those lines , there’s so many flavours of them.

But the point here might be that in ZFC , (functional) extensionality is an axiom, in Lean it is a theorem . So if you count axioms as a defeq, then maybe that. But I don’t think it’s defined well.

if you meant “in the proof assistant that use set theory, what would defeq mean ?” — and the answer might be they don’t have this concept well defined

well, norfl for "the proof assistant that use set theory" then?

Jiaxi Mo said:

Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 said:

Jiaxi Mo said:

just a naive question. what would be "defeq" in ZFC?

if you meant “in the proof assistant that use set theory, what would defeq mean ?” — and the answer might be they don’t have this concept well defined

well, norfl for "the proof assistant that use set theory" then?

Yea that is really the crux of the issue. There is so much annoying nuance in that ..how tf is your theorem prover both avoiding using type theory, and is checked by a computer!? This is typically resolved by considering things like FoL and others almost part of both type theory and axiomatic set theory/ classical mathematics.

No rfl is indeed fairly relevant, but remember how rfl works in spirit, it reduces expressions to some primitive form(and eval is even less applicable). But, you require your theory to be strongly normalisable and get into weird technical stuff again, and if you tried this with ZFC since there are so many axioms and the asserted existence of one object everything is essentially in, Set, you are essentially reducing to the axioms + FoL in some sense (and as I mention later, the FoL part cannot be talked in terms of Set hence this is a big difference between the fuller integration into type theory and Lean).

That's why I said, if you consider axioms as part of defeq yes, but again there is so much nuance and technicalities I just overlooked there, it would take a lot of terminology and dissection to get a suitable answer I think.

You can argue Lean is somehow also reducing to axioms, but I think that really overlooks how Lean works, and the notion of axiom, since the 3 supposed axioms are one thing, and then there is a huge amount of bells and whistles almost considered baked into "rules of inference" . Lean can also actually talk about propositions and logical operations as objects, whereas in ZFC you cannot say the logical implication or the FoL part of it can also be expressed in Sets.

Something like Lean has homoiconicity, or Lean is its own metalogic theory, honestly the deeper this rabbit hole goes the chance of anyone stumbling onto this who knows this properly and can/wants to give insight rapidly goes to 0 lmao.

You can argue Lean is somehow also reducing to axioms, but I think that really overlooks how Lean works, and the notion of axiom, since the 3 supposed axioms are one thing, and then there is a huge amount of bells and whistles almost considered baked into "rules of inference" .

I'd like to ask the following question: What about switching from different axioms? from ZFC to DTT for instance? @Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦

Amlal El Mahrouss said:

You can argue Lean is somehow also reducing to axioms, but I think that really overlooks how Lean works, and the notion of axiom, since the 3 supposed axioms are one thing, and then there is a huge amount of bells and whistles almost considered baked into "rules of inference" .

I'd like to ask the following question: What about switching from different axioms? from ZFC to DTT for instance? Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦

That's the thing, it fundamentally does not work that way. DTT kind of..has no axioms? Lean has expressed AXIOMS in DTT, 3 of them, in order to use DTT + those axioms to study math better.

But, what does DTT have? I mean it has rules it must abide by ..right? And in essence are those not axioms then?

That's when you get into the fact "rules of inference" vs "axioms" remains murky, context dependent, and arguable to this day AFAIK.

Note also this is CIC not simple DTT, and its easy to argue the CIC part is also axioms on vanilla DTT? The axioms asserting the existence and such of inductive types themselves, which are not explicitly treated as Pi, Sigma , or function types from DTT.

It is a bit like asking , what are the "axioms" of FoL, and then ZFC axioms are expressed in FoL , which is in itself meta to the actual set theory.

So one could ask, are the axioms of ZFC, the ones youre thinking of? Or are they actually just somehow "axioms" of FoL also, and it becomes kind of weird fast.
Yeah I understand that part, I just wanted to make sure I got the correct info.

Unfortunately, unless I am wrong and someone can be bothered, its unlikely you get the other way, that someone simply comes to voluntarily and randomly endorse the opinion as correct, as their contribution to the thread.

I'm not an expert in set theory either (and far from becoming one), so I'd love to stay tuned on that part as well.
Speaking of statistics, It's probably more than a few-lifetimes, because of how deep the problem runs. I certainly hope to witness that in my lifetime though.

I suggest broadly googling, Cntrl + F in various Lean/type theory books, the stuff we talk about yourself as much as you can.

And if you find ambiguity and things you think I said that are blatantly wrong, I would also love to know that and have you share the rare gem you found the info in. Because this stuff is so esoteric.

Bear in mind, it is also esoteric, because the vast vast majority of mathematicians, including those considered the very best in the world, really do not care about this stuff , it sits on a layer way too strange and fundamental.

Kind of by proxy, you do not need extremely technical insight into this to do such "elite" math, and almost in all practical aspects.

I cannot stress to you how little pragmatic benefit Lean has been in my life , how few care in math academia around me despite however hard i try engage interest in it, it is really a HUGE opportunity cost.

All that to say, don't consider these things to give you any sort of practical or pragmatic leg up or esoteric rare insight, even though its so esoteric and abstract so you may think it can from a distance.

But if it interests you, do it for that sake, which is why I do it and hence that isn't an issue, id more want others to do it because i want to share said enjoyment.
